[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S7-01] Notes are question-based: what, why, how, who/whom, when/where, evidence, reasoning, insights, differences, limitations and exceptions, conclusion, chosen by the content. Three depths: quick essence, understand, deep dive. 'The book does not say' where the book is silent. Every statement links to its source page. What the book says and what is new now are kept apart; an update carries its source link and checked date.
[S7-02] Visuals in notes are drawn by code from the content type: process as a flow, dates as a timeline, comparison as a difference table, numbers as a chart, cause and effect as a relationship diagram, main idea and branches as a concept map.

pages.question: Gold-backed paper currency ko value kaise milti thi?
pages.essence: Note ki value paper se nahi, fixed gold redemption ke promise se aati thi. [p004-i1]
answer: Gold-backed note ko demand par fixed quantity of gold mein exchange kiya ja sakta tha; paper ki apni intrinsic value bahut kam thi. [p004-i1]
Central bank gold reserves rakhta aur paper notes issue karta tha; holder in principle notes dekar fixed gold le sakta tha. [p004-i2]
Har note ke liye gold backing ki requirement excessive money printing ko limit karti thi. [p004-i2]
deep_dive: Do cheezein alag rakho: paper kis material ka hai, aur issuer uske badle kya dene ka promise karta hai. Yahan purchasing value ka base doosri cheez—gold redemption—hai. [p004-i1]
‘In principle’ qualification important hai: supplied text exchange ka principle batata hai, har historical situation mein actual access ki guarantee nahi. [p004-i2]

Limited legal tender prescribed limit tak compulsory hai; usse upar acceptance voluntary hai. Book Coinage Act, 2011 cite karti hai. [p005, p005-i6]

₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 aur ₹20 coins ki legal-tender limit ₹1,000 tak hai. 50 paise coin ki limit ₹10 tak hai. Below 50 paise coins demonetized hain, legal tender nahi. [p005, p005-i9, p005-i10, p005-i11]

deep_dive.text: ‘Unlimited’ validity ki condition nahi hatata. ‘Limited’ ka matlab limit ke upar payment prohibited nahi; acceptance voluntary hai. ₹1,000 limit listed coins se total payment amount ki hai, ₹1,000 denomination ke coin ki nahi.

caption.text: Limited legal tender: prescribed limit ke upar acceptance voluntary.
